reader.requirement: A STOP RUN statement, or an EXIT PROGRAM statement executed in a called program, transfers control outside the program and has no next executable statement (nothing after it runs: STOP RUN ends the run unit even from a called program, EXIT PROGRAM returns to the caller); an EXIT PROGRAM in a program not under control of a CALL does not transfer control out and continues with the next statement (§1985:X.5.4.4 GR1).

edition-consulted.switches: the STOP RUN WITH NORMAL/ERROR STATUS phrase is refused below 2002 (COBOL0900); plain STOP RUN and EXIT PROGRAM take the same emission at every edition

reader.edition-search: StatementEmitter.Visit(BoundStop) and CallEmitter.EmitExitProgram consult no edition (read in full); the __asCalled activation flag, not the edition, chooses EXIT PROGRAM's return or continue
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: STOP RUN and EXIT PROGRAM transfer out the same way; 2002+ add GOBACK and the WITH STATUS / RAISING phrases, which 1985 refuses
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses end main programs with STOP RUN; STOP RUN inside a called program, EXIT PROGRAM in a called program followed by unreachable statements, and EXIT PROGRAM in a main program are not exercised at 85

probes.printed: SUBB B1 / AFTER SUBB (SUBB's B2 never runs); AFTER MAIN EXIT PROGRAM (main's EXIT PROGRAM continues); SUBC STOP RUN then nothing (the caller's following DISPLAY never runs); exit 0; EXPECT MATCH
probes.expected: EXIT PROGRAM in a called program returns to the caller; STOP RUN in a called program ends the run unit; EXIT PROGRAM in the main program continues (§1985:X.5.4.4 GR1)

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: STOP RUN WITH status requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: the WITH STATUS phrase is not in the 1985 STOP format; refused

OK  §1985:X.5.4.4 GR1  (5.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: STOP RUN emits throw StopRun, unwound to the run-unit entry whatever the call depth; EXIT PROGRAM emits ProgramReturn guarded by __asCalled, so it returns only from a called activation. Both probed at --std 85.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85, EXPECT MATCH. E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-220/src/r2.cob: EXIT PROGRAM in a called program reached under that program's own PERFORM returns to the caller's PERFORMed paragraph and nothing after it runs; STOP RUN in a USE declarative of a called program ends the run unit (caller's next DISPLAY never runs, exit 0). E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-220/src/r3.cob: EXIT PROGRAM from a USE declarative of a program CALLed from a SORT INPUT PROCEDURE returns to the CALL and the SORT continues (IP AFTER SUBU / OUT AAAA / OUT CCCC / AFTER SORT) at 85; at --std 2023 the same program prints SUBU USE 10 / AFTER SORT (the 2002+ SORT-termination rule), so the edition arm is real and the 1985 arm is right. The reader's edition-consulted list missed that arm. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.4.2 GRL2.4; OK §1985:X.5.4.4 GR2.
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/CodeGen/DispatchEmitter.cs#EmitRunUseBody: DialectLevel >= 2002 adds the UseProcedureExitFilter on ProgramReturn leaving a declarative (SORT termination when an EXIT PROGRAM leaves a USE procedure during another element's SORT); the 1985 arm omits it, so the SORT continues
